# Cadenza

Cadenza lets you **show your work** to your human and **ask them questions**. They see it on their phone or laptop and answer there.
Use it instead of long chat summaries whenever a picture, page, chart or short video explains the result faster.

## When to use it

- You finished something visible or reviewable: show it (pick a template).
- You need a decision: ask, then keep working and wait in the background.
- Before a large change: show a `plan`.
- At the end of a task: `cadenza done`.

## Commands

All commands print short JSON. Pass file paths, never file contents.

- `cadenza show --title "Checkout redesign" --template ui-change --data '{"summary": "…", "after": {"file": "./after.png"}}'`
  Show work: a filled template or files. Starts or continues a thread. Safe to retry with the same retry_id.
- `cadenza show --title "Perf report" ./report.html ./demo.mp4`
  Files instead of a template: one post, one attachment per file.
- `cadenza ask "Keep the promo field visible?" --choice yes --choice no --waiting`
  Ask the owner a question, optionally with choices. Returns the question id at once; use wait to get the answer.
- `cadenza wait q_123 --timeout 30m`
  Wait for an answer to a question. The server holds the request up to 30 s; call again to keep waiting.
- `cadenza responses`
  Everything the owner sent since the last acknowledged check: what to do next, then each reply.
- `cadenza reply r_123 "fixed in round 2"`
  Answer one of the owner's comments, e.g. "fixed in round 2".
- `cadenza done --summary "Checkout redesign shipped"`
  Mark a thread ready for review: the work is finished.
- `cadenza threads`
  List threads. For an agent: open threads on its machine, which it may continue.
- `cadenza templates`, `cadenza templates ui-change`
  List templates.
- `cadenza make-template ./my-template.json`
  Create a custom template from blocks. Usable at once, no approval.

## Templates (preferred)

Built in: ui-change, feature-demo, bug-fix, code-change, test-report, perf-compare, data-report, experiment, options, plan,
research, design-review, progress, incident, release-notes.

Run `cadenza templates <name>` once to see a template's slots, guide and example, then fill it with `--data`
(JSON, or `--data @file.json`). Image, video and file slots take `{"file": "<path>"}`. If a slot is wrong, the
error says exactly how to fix it. The `options` template also asks a question whose choices are the options.
No template fits? Make one with `cadenza make-template` (usable at once) or show plain files.

## Files

Cadenza converts what it can before uploading: PNG/JPEG/GIF become WebP, MP4 is made fast-start. A webpage must be
**one self-contained HTML file** (inline its CSS, JS and images); it runs with no network access. Other video needs
ffmpeg; the error prints the exact command. Secrets (.env, keys) are refused.

## Asking and waiting

`cadenza ask` returns a question id at once. Do not sit idle: keep working on what does not depend on the answer, and
run `cadenza wait <id>` **in the background** (pick your own `--timeout`, or none). Exit codes:
0 answered (the answer is printed), 2 still open at your timeout (wait again or carry on), 3 dismissed, 4 replaced by a
newer question, 5 Cadenza unreachable (decide yourself what to do; Cadenza never decides for you).
Use `--replaces <id>` to replace an older open question instead of asking twice.

## Replies

`cadenza responses` prints one sentence saying what to do next, then everything your human sent: answers, notes,
approve or request-changes, comments pinned to a line or spot, sketches, photos. Attached files are saved under
`.cadenza/responses/`. Act on each item; for comments, answer with `cadenza reply <id> <text>`.
Posts are final: to change something, show a new version (e.g. title "Round 2: fixes your 2 comments").

## Threads

One thread per task. `show` and `ask` continue your latest open thread; use `--new` for a new task or
`--thread <id>` to continue one from `cadenza threads` (e.g. after /clear). Every call is safe to retry.

## Notifications

Your human is notified for questions, finished tasks and new work (at most every few minutes per thread). Use
`--notify-title` to give a short title such as "Checkout redesign: keep promo field visible?".
